As the chip drops toward the stack a copy frame appears automatically right under the chip and captures A, B and C; a thumbnail shows all three. Caption 'the first shader that reads the screen triggers the copy'.

B15.visual_intent: Three transparent sheets stacked in isometric view, labelled 'layer -1', 'layer 0', 'layer 1' (a small note 'a CanvasLayer node'). B17.capture_spec: C08: capture_scenes.gd id C08 (three squares and window; BackBufferCopy with copy_mode Rect at its default rect, node at (100,100); copy_mode set to Viewport at 9.0 s); 14.5 s planned, 30 fps, Forward+. MUST run in a fresh Godot process (the black needs an empty back buffer). 1:1 ROUTE, not the 4K route: a Rect box is measured in render pixels (run-13: on the 4K route the default box is only 34 canvas units), so capture_scene.sh renders C08 in the 1280 x 720 window itself, where the default box is the 100 px corner of the screen (run-10), and enlarges the frames 3x by whole pixels. The corner patch is 38 x 38 px in the window (0.578 to 0.608 of the frame's width, 0.078 to 0.131 of its height); the rect does not follow the node.
B17.visual_intent: The three squares and the window, with the node in Rect mode at its defaults: the window is black except a tiny stage-coloured patch at its top-left corner (the only part copied). At 9 s the mode is switched to Viewport and the window fills with A, B and C. Readouts 'Rect mode' then 'Viewport'; one terracotta ring on the tiny patch.
B17.motion_claim: A black window with a tiny patch fills with the three squares when the mode becomes Viewport.

show.event: readout 'Rect mode'; window black
ring on the corner patch
readout 'Viewport'; window shows A, B, C

B17.runner_up: ShaderLab with the pond and the reflection
B17.why: The black window shows 'undefined' literally and keeps this act's cast; the pond version is verified too but shows only a missing reflection.
